question.worked_solution:
First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying both sides by $2.$ We must make sure that all of the terms on the right-hand side are multiplied by $2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3h-4}{2} & =2-h \\ 2\cdot (\frac{3h-4}{2}) & =2\cdot (2-h) \\ \cancel{2}\cdot (\frac{3h-4}{\cancel{2}}) & =2\cdot 2-2\cdot h \\ 3h-4 & =4-2h\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve the remaining equation using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}3h-4 & =4-2h \\ 3h-4+2h & =4-2h+2h \\ 5h-4 & =4 \\ 5h-4+4 & =4+4 \\ 5h & =8 \\ \frac{5h}{5} & =\frac{8}{5} \\ h & =\frac{8}{5}\end{aligned}
$$
